# Molar — overview for readers and agents

Updated September 5, 2026.

Molar is a beta browser automation and QA platform. Its homepage explains testing for web apps, particularly flows involving third-party services. The broader browser platform is described at https://molar.it/platform.

## What problem does Molar address?

A customer task can fail even when the individual systems appear healthy. A payment may succeed while the order remains pending because a webhook was not handled. An account may be created while its verification email never arrives. Molar brings browser execution, supported stateful test services and run evidence into the same testing workflow.

## How does the product fit together?

Cartographer explores application states and supports flow mapping and Playwright export workflows. Clones provides repeatable service behavior for supported payment, email, SMS, identity and storage scenarios. Guard connects checks to release and recurring workflows. Trace collects browser evidence for investigation. Mender is a repair workflow in preview.

These are product responsibilities, not a guarantee that every connected workflow is available for every app. Browser execution, generated-test replay, repository publication and repair verification are distinct outcomes. Confirm supported scope in a beta setup.

Product pages:
- https://molar.it/products/cartographer
- https://molar.it/products/clones
- https://molar.it/products/guard
- https://molar.it/products/trace
- https://molar.it/products/mender

## What are service Clones?

Clones lets a configured test environment use controlled third-party service behavior. Core stateful services cover Stripe, Twilio, email, auth and S3 scenarios. Other catalog entries provide narrower fixture coverage. Neither a core service nor a fixture implies complete parity with its real vendor. Inspect the endpoint and scenario coverage required by your application.

Your app must be configured to use the intended test services and identities. Merely using Molar does not automatically isolate every external side effect. See https://molar.it/docs/clones/ and https://molar.it/security.

## Can people and coding agents use Molar?

Molar has a dashboard and developer interfaces including CLI and MCP. Setup, authentication, target authorization and supported task scope still apply. Use the canonical documentation at https://docs.molar.it for current installation instructions and command syntax. The marketing site is an introduction, not an API contract.

## Are the website demos live tests?

No. They are explicitly labeled illustrative walkthroughs. The checkout example compares a healthy flow with a missing webhook so visitors can inspect the relationship between a browser action, payment state, order confirmation and receipt. No actual payment or message is sent by that demo.

The separate https://molar.it/verify page uses the existing Instant Proof service. Its current availability, limits and result state are shown in the interface.

## How much does Molar cost?

Molar is in beta. The website does not advertise fixed plan prices, unlimited usage or a free-run allowance. Discuss workflows, services, environments and run volume at https://molar.it/pricing or https://molar.it/contact.

## Where should I start?

- QA overview: https://molar.it/
- General browser platform: https://molar.it/platform
- Sign up: https://app.molar.it/dashboard/signup
- Sign in: https://app.molar.it/dashboard/login
- Documentation: https://docs.molar.it
- Practical guides: https://molar.it/blog
- Company: https://molar.it/company
- Privacy: https://molar.it/privacy
- Terms: https://molar.it/terms

For a specific application, start with a scoped flow, an authorized test environment, the services it touches and a clear expected outcome. Review the observed evidence and any coverage limitations before relying on a result.
